name: Universal perfboard sheet, 9 x 15 cm
summary: Plain 90 x 150 x 1.6 mm prototyping sheet: a 2.54 mm grid of holes, each ringed by its own isolated solder pad.
description: A generic 90 × 150 mm perfboard sheet with isolated copper pads. Hole placement is schematic; the solid export keeps the sheet envelope.
source: Checked by web search plus the Wikipedia perfboard article: sheets sold as 9 x 15 cm perfboard are listed at exactly 90 x 150 mm with a 2.54 mm (0.1 in) hole grid, and Wikipedia gives 2.54 mm as the standard perfboard grid with holes ringed by round or square copper pads. Retailer listings for this size quote a 1.00 mm drill, so 1.0 mm is a typical hole, not a pad - listings I found do not publish one pad diameter, and pad shape, single- or double-sided copper, laminate (FR-2 phenolic or FR-4) and hole count all vary by maker. Thickness is not part of the 9 x 15 cm standard either: a listing for this exact sheet gives 1.5 mm, while this entry uses the 1.6 mm named in its variant, so check your own sheet with calipers before cutting a recess. The preview shows holes and isolated copper pads; the exported solid is a plain 90 x 150 x 1.6 mm sheet with the 90 mm side along X. The preview adds a schematic 2.54 mm contact layout, not a manufacturer-specific drill pattern. The export is the body envelope.
